correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the derivations and rank proof for all finite fields: cubic defining relations force D(x),D(y)∈m even in char 2, yielding exactly q^10 derivations. The 5×5 restriction on m has blocks (A,0;B,T_A) with B freely chosen and the induced Sym² block T_A. Its rank is s+t+rank(ker A→coker T_A), with exactly q^{6-(2-s)(3-t)}R_q(3-t,2-s,j) choices of B at rank increment j. For odd q the A-rank/T_A-rank multiplicities are (0,0):1,(1,2):L,(2,2):q²(q−1),(2,3):G−q²(q−1); for even q they are (0,0):1,(1,1):L,(2,0):q−1,(2,1):G−q+1. Independent symbolic check det(T_A)=4(a+d)(ad−bc), integer polynomial normalization H_q(1)=q^10 in both characteristics, exhaustive independent direct Leibniz-matrix/rank enumeration for 1024 F2 and 59049 F3 operators, and full linear-block enumeration for prime q=2,3,5,7 agree with both formulas. This is an all-q analytic proof, not extrapolation of finite tests. The maximum rank 5 for odd q and 3 for even q follows; in char2 every D annihilates 1,x²,y².

value.rationale: The algebra k[x,y]/(x,y)^3 is the first two-variable total-degree jet algebra retaining all three quadratic monomials; its derivation representation is an intrinsic and natural invariant. The theorem classifies every possible linear rank and its precise frequency over every finite field, not merely dimension(Der) or a couple of small cases. The characteristic-two collapse in maximal attainable rank (5 to 3), forced fixed powers, and full-rank-on-the-maximal-ideal existence in odd characteristic are structural statements likely useful as comparison data for local algebra, jet-scheme and derivation research. The argument uses elementary finite linear algebra, but no inspected source renders this exact all-q invariant a textbook substitution or a known table. It makes no assertion about automorphism orbits or Jordan types.

limitations: Rank on the original six-dimensional commutative algebra only, not adjoint ranks, automorphism orbits, Jordan classifications, higher jet orders or all local Artinian rings.
Small-field exhaustive enumerations are supporting cross-checks; the infinite prime-power scope follows from the algebraic block argument.
Bibliographic comparison establishes best-of-knowledge originality, not a guarantee of priority or independence from every unindexed older theorem.
